subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default for both new and already-persisted jobs, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain invalid and one-shot-only?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects upgrade behavior, existing scheduled jobs, and session retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted/load or doctor coverage for omitted existing jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict one-shot-only contract and rework or close this defaulting PR after documenting recovery for existing jobs.

options.title: Accept fresh-create only
options.body: Land only the new-job default and explicitly own that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted/load or doctor coverage for omitted existing jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and recent history points to steipete on that boundary.
